3903:
** παρασκευάζω**,
_future_ **-άσω**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.18}} (but _3rd.pers._ _singular_ **-σκευᾷ**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 14.2}}, _2nd pers._ _plural_ **-σκευᾶτε**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|“SIG” 1106.113 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC))}}: _Ionic dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_ _pluperfect_ _passive_ παρεσκευάδατο {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.218, etc.}}: later sometimes **παρασκεάζω**, as παρεσκεασμένων {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“IPE” 12.32 B 12 (Olbia, 3rd c.BC)}}:—
3914:
** παραχειμ-άζω**,
_perfect_ _participle_ **-κεχειμακώς**{{NT|NT.Act.28.11}}:—**winter at** a place, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 260, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.8, 56.30, “Periplus Maris Rubri [1st c.AD]” 32, etc.; π. ἐν πόλει 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sertorius” 3.}}
3915:
** παραχειμ-ᾰσία**, ἡ,
**wintering in** a place, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.35.1, “SIG” 762.16 (Odessus, 1st c.BC), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.38, NT.Act.27.12; ἐνταῦθα τὴν π. ἐποιεῖτο 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.28.}}
3920:
** παρείσ-ακτος**, ον,
**introduced privily,** {{NT+1st c.BC+|NT.Gal.2.4: nickname of Ptolemy XI, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 17.1.8.}}
3923:
** παρεισ-φέρω**,
**bring in beside**, π. νόμον **propose** an **amending** law, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.88, compare 99 (_passive_)}}; **smuggle in,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|PTeb. 38.12(2nd c.BC)}}: generally, **introduce**, Στωϊκὰς δόξας {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 213.9; τρόπον Aps. p.243H.}}; **apply besides**, σπουδήν {{NT|NT.2Pet.1.5}}; **interpolate**, {{Refs|Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.29H.}}:—_passive_, **to be brought in**, χυτρῖδες εἰς τὰς μέθας -φέρονται {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 110.}}
3927:
** παρεπί-δημος**, ον,
**sojourning in a strange place**, especially as _substantive_, {{LXX+3rd c.BC+|LXX.Gen.23.4, “PPetr.” 3 P. 14 (3rd c.BC), 3rd c.BC(?): Callixinus Historicus 2, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 32.6.4, etc.}}
3932:
** παρθεν-εία**, ἡ,
**virginity**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 592, “Tr.” 980}}:—more frequently **παρθενία**, _Epic dialect_ **παρθενίη**, {{LXX+7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 102, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).48, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 898 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1487 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 894b35, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.502, LXX.Jer.3.4, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 26.2, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.30}}; ἀπὸ τῆς π. or ἀπὸπ., {{NT|NT.Luke.2.36, “IG” 12(7).395.20 (from Amorgos)}}; ἐκ π. {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Brutus” 13, “PSI” 1.41.5 (4th c.AD)}}; of a man, {{Refs|Ach. Tat. 5.20.}}

3937:
**Παρμενᾶς**, ᾶ, ὁ
**Parmenas**: Act.6:5.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3940:
** παροικ-ία**, ἡ,
(πάροικος {{Refs|11)}} **sojourning** in a foreign land, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Wis.19.10, NT.Act.13.17}}; οἱ ἐν τῇ π., ={οἱ ἐκτός}, {{Refs|LXX “Si.Prol.”}}
3955:
** παρρησι-άζομαι**,
_future_ **-άσομαι**{{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 156a, etc. (but παρρησιασθήσομαι LXX.Job.22.26)}}: _aorist_ ἐπαρρησιασάμην {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.1, uncertain in 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.80}}: _perfect_ (see.below): used only in Prose:—**speak freely, openly**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 487d}}; τι{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. work] 491e, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator [prev. cited]; πρὸς ὑμᾶς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 178a, etc.; τινὶ περί τινος [prev. author] “Chrm.” 156a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.177; πολλὰ κατά τινος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.13.8:}}_perfect_ πεπαρρησίασμαι in _active_ sense, ἂ γιγνώσκω πάνθ᾽ ἁπλῶς.. πεπ. {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.51, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus}} [prev. cited]; but τὰ πεπαρρησιασμένα in _passive_ sense, **free expressions**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.10; -ασμέναι φωναί 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.4 O.:}} —once in _active_ {{Refs|[prev. work] p.58 O.}}
3959:
**Πάταρα**, -ων, τὰ
**Patara, a maritime city of Lycia**: Act.21:1.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3963:
**Πάτμος**, -ου, ἡ
**Patmos, an island in the Ægean Sea**: Rev.1:9.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3964:
** πατρ-ᾰλοίας**,
_genitive_ α and ου, ὁ, _vocative_ -αλοῖα: (άω):— **one who slays** or **strikes his father, parricide**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 911, 1327, “Ra.” 274, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114a, “Sph.” 241d, etc.: as _feminine_, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 10.38}}:—sometimes written **πατραλῴας** or **πατρολῴας**(πατρ-λώας, πατρ-λόας) in codices, as {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.1Tim.1.9, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 16.11.1.}}
3969:
**Πατρόβας**, -ᾶ, ὁ
**Patrobas**: Rom.16:14.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3970:
** πατρο-παράδοτος**, ον,
**handed down from one's fathers, inherited**, ἡ μικρὰ καὶ π. οὐσία {{NT+2nd c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.48; ἡ π. ἡγεμονία 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.4; ἀναστροφή NT.1Pet.1.18; Ζεύς “OGI” 331.49 (Pergam., 2nd c.BC), παρέχεσθαι π. τὰν εὔνοιαν “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2134b4 (probably), compare “IG” 12 (5).860.4 (from Tenos).}}

2. **the Apostle Paul** (cf. Σαῦλος): Act.13:9, and frequently throughout Ac., Rom.1:1, 1Co.1:1, al., 2Pe.3:15.
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3974: **Paphos **, a town in Cyprus celebrated for its temple of Aphrodite, {{8th/7th c.BC|Odyssey by Homer}}:—;_adjective_ πάφιος, η, ον, of Aphrodite, {{5th/4th c.BC|Aristophanes Comicus}} (Middle Liddel)
3980:
** πειθαρχ-έω**,
**obey one in authority**, _absolutely_, πειθαρχεῖ.., ἄπληκτος ὥσπερ ἵππος {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 232, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1262b3: mostly with _dative_, π. πατρί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1178; τοῖς νόμοισι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 762; τοῖς ἐφεστῶσι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.19, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 538d}}; ὡς ἂν.. τοῖς πηδαλίοις ἡ ναῦς π. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 139; τοῖς προσταχθεῖσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.13; τῷ λόγῳ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1295b6: with _genitive_ (compare πείθω 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.3), ἐπιταγμάτων Epist. Darei in “SIG” 22.7 (5th c.BC)}}; στρατηγοῦ {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“OGI” 12.11 (Priene, 3rd c.BC), compare 244.38 (Syria, 2nd c.BC)}}; τινος {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“PGiss.” 2.16 (2nd c.BC)}}:—_middle_, ἔθνος.. πειθαρχέεσθαι ἑτοῖμον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.91.}}
3990:
** πελεκ-ίζω**,
**cut off with an axe**, especially **behead**, τινα {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.7.12, 11.30.2 (_passive_), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 16.2.18, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.101, NT.Rev.20.4 (_passive_).}}
3994:
** πενθερ-ά**,
_Ionic dialect_ **πενθερή**, ἡ, _feminine_ of πενθερός, **mother-in-law**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.70, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 149, NT.Mark.1.30, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 8, etc.}}
3998:
** πενιχρ-ός**, ά, όν,
**poor, needy**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.348, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 49, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 165, 181, 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.23, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.19.}}—poetical word, found in Comedy texts, as [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 976, {5-6th c.BC}: Philetaerus Comicus 4, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Diodorus Epigrammaticus Comedy texts 2.8, in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 578a}}], and in later Prose, as {{LXX+5th c.BC+|“PPetr.” 3p.73 (3rd c.BC), 5th-4th c.BC: Socratis et Socraticorum Epistulae cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.13.64, LXX.Exo.22.25, etc.; π. δίαιτα 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ οἰκονομίας” p.48 “J.”}}: _comparative_ πενιχρότερος {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.284}}, _superlative_ **-ότατος**{{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.21.7}}. _adverb_ **-χρῶς**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1252b3 [ῐ}}.by nature, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus and 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” cc., also 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 2.416, elsewhere ῑ by position.]}}
3999:
** πεντάκῐς** [ᾰ],
_adverb_ **five times**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.19, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 323, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 242, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.5}}:—later **πεντάκῐ**, {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 3.56, “Anthologia Graeca” 13.15, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.80 P., +others}}
